title: Making a simple drawer box from plywood
subtitle: Cut, assemble, and fit a five-piece plywood drawer box with a rebated base panel for a kitchen or furniture project
excerpt: How to make a simple plywood drawer box. Covers calculating sizes from the cabinet opening, cutting the front, back, sides, and base, assembling with butt joints or rebated joints, and fitting drawer runners.
sourceNotes: Newey and Drage, Practical Carpentry and Joinery (referenced, not reproduced). Cassell's Cyclopaedia of Mechanics (referenced, not reproduced). Collins Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced).

glossaryTerms.definition: The five-piece structural box (two sides, a front, a back, and a base) that forms the functional part of a drawer. A separate false front (the visible face panel) is attached to the drawer box front later. Plywood is the standard material for a robust drawer box.

The sliding mechanism that carries the drawer box in and out of the cabinet. Side-mount runners attach to the sides of the cabinet and the drawer-box sides. Undermount runners attach beneath the drawer box and are hidden from view. Both require precise sizing of the drawer box width to give the correct clearance.

content.text: is a simple five-piece box: two sides, a front, a back, and a rebated-in base. The sizing depends on the
type. Get the width right for the runners and the height right for the opening before cutting anything else.

Measure the cabinet opening width and the runner clearance. For standard 450 mm full-extension side-mount runners, the drawer box width = opening width minus 25 mm (12.5 mm each side). For undermount runners, check the manufacturer's specification (usually opening width minus 0-3 mm). The drawer box height = opening height minus 10-25 mm clearance. The drawer box depth = 25 mm less than the cabinet depth to allow for the false front. Use 12 mm or 18 mm birch plywood for the sides, front, and back; 6 mm plywood or MDF for the base.

Mark all parts accurately with a pencil and a combination square. Cut to size with a circular saw or jigsaw (or hand saw for small boxes). Cut a groove or rebate in the inside bottom edge of all four sides to accept the base panel: a 6 mm-wide groove at 6 mm up from the bottom edge allows the base to slide in. This is cleanest with a router but a table saw or repeated saw cuts also work. The base slides in from the back before the back piece is fitted.

Glue and screw the front to the two side pieces first (PVA and 40 mm countersunk screws from the front into the side ends). Check the assembly is square before the glue sets by measuring the diagonals; they must be equal. Slide the base into the groove from the back. Glue and screw the back piece to close the box. Allow to dry overnight under clamps. Sand the outside faces smooth.
Fit the runners and hang the drawer

Fix the cabinet sections of the runners to the cabinet sides at the correct height, using a spirit level to keep them horizontal. Attach the drawer sections of the runners to the drawer box sides. Slide the drawer into the cabinet. The drawer should run smoothly with no side play. Attach the false front to the drawer box front with two screws from inside; adjust its position while the screws are loose before tightening.

attrs.symptom: Drawer binds and sticks halfway through the travel
attrs.cause: The box is slightly racked (not square) or the runner is not level.
attrs.fix: Check the drawer box diagonals and check the runner level. Plane or sand the binding face of the drawer box side very slightly.

attrs.symptom: Base panel rattles or flexes under load
attrs.cause: The base groove is too wide, or the base is too thin for the span.
attrs.fix: Run a bead of PVA glue along the bottom edge of the base panel where it sits in the groove. For a large drawer, use 9 mm plywood for the base.
